name: freeze-v1
status: Content of git tag freeze-v1. Never edited after the tag. A change is a new, disclosed version recorded in DECISIONS.md. freeze-v2 adds only the IEEE-CIS feature preprocessing (data.ieee_cis.features_freeze_v2), in a separate file; this file stays as it is.
purpose: Everything that is fixed before any fraud-data (ULB, IEEE-CIS) result exists, for both fraud datasets; only the IEEE-CIS feature preprocessing is fixed later, in freeze-v2. Choices made with labels use ADBench only.

detectors.params_note: PyOD defaults, except PCA min_variance_ratio (components with explained-variance ratio <= 1e-10 are dropped; a documented modification of PyOD's PCA). contamination is unused: no detector threshold is used.
detectors.ecod: train-only re-implementation: ECDFs and skewness signs fixed at fit time (PyOD 3.6.7 ECOD is batch-dependent)
detectors.knn_lof_training_scores: leave-one-out (a row is not its own neighbour); PyOD's own behaviour

knn_lof_fit_sample.seed: split seed; 0 when the split has none (ULB, IEEE-CIS)

detectors.knn_lof_fallback: IEEE-CIS only: if one KNN or LOF scoring pass takes more than 30 minutes, the fit sample becomes 10,000 rows (Master Plan, Risks); disclosed if used
detectors.score_direction: higher = more anomalous for every detector

E-bench.source: lowest average FP@K rank among the 20 triples, min-max + mean, 15 ADBench sets, 2% budget (supervisor, 2026-10-29)
E-bench.note: identical to E-lit: the benchmark rule selected the published default. Evaluated once and reported under both names. Friedman over the 20 triples: p 0.976 (2%), 0.419 (5%), all within the Nemenyi CD, so the triples cannot be told apart

E-bench-5%.source: the E-bench rule at the 5% ADBench budget; descriptive

E-all.source: all six detectors: the 'bigger is better?' control; descriptive

ensemble_selection_evidence.files: results/tables/e2/ebench.md, e2_summary.csv, e2_friedman.csv (rebuilt by python -m thesis.e2 and python -m thesis.ebench)

fusion.calibrators: fitted per member on that member's training scores only (ULB day 1, IEEE-CIS month 1); min-max not clipped; percentile = share of training scores <= s

ieee_cis.primary_source: student's decision: the budget E-bench was selected at, and the closest to the IEEE-CIS fraud rate

common.rule: threshold = numpy.quantile(training scores, q) (method 'linear'); alert if score > threshold
common.fitted_on: each method's own training scores (fused training scores for ensembles); never refitted
common.methods: the six singles (IForest per seed) and the four ensembles; all six fusion configs for ensembles, the primary one reported first

ulb.check: alert rate and FPR on day 2 vs 1 - q

ieee_cis.check: monthly alert rate and FPR vs 1 - q (E4, H3a)

rules.k_definition: K = max(1, ceil(budget * n)), n = rows in the evaluated window (or bootstrap resample), with budget * n rounded to 9 decimals first
rules.ties: expected value: rows tied with the K-th score share the remaining alert slots in proportion, so row order never decides an alert
rules.zero_variance_member: under z-score calibration a member with constant training scores (range exactly 0) is mapped to 0
rules.zero_variance_member_status: mapped to 0; occurred in 0 of 450 ADBench and 0 of 10 ULB day-1 members (thesis.zero_variance @8b25943)

adbench.source: Minqi824/ADBench classical .npz files at the commit pinned in src/thesis/download.py
adbench.selection_rule: 1,000-50,000 rows, at most 100 features, anomaly rate at most 10%, 13_fraud excluded (it is ULB)
adbench.duplicates: kept (files as distributed); duplicate-aware robustness check with --dedup; not a full reproduction of the ADBench protocol

ulb.features: V1-V28 and log1p(Amount); Time is the split variable only
ulb.split: day 1 (Time < 86400 s) fit, day 2 test; every training row strictly earlier than every test row
ulb.duplicates: kept (file as distributed), as on ADBench

ieee_cis.source: Kaggle ieee-fraud-detection, train_transaction.csv (the test files have no released labels)
ieee_cis.time: day d = floor((TransactionDT - min TransactionDT) / 86400); month 1 = days 0-29, month m = days 30(m-1) to 30m-1 for m = 2-5, month 6 = day 150 onwards
ieee_cis.split: month 1 fit (detectors, preprocessing, calibrators, thresholds); months 2-6 test, one window per month; every training row strictly earlier than every test row; no calibration window
ieee_cis.features_freeze_v2: fixed in freeze-v2, from month-1 data only and without labels, before any IEEE-CIS score is compared with labels; freeze-v2 changes nothing else

data.preprocessing: z-score of every detector input with training-split statistics (constant columns get scale 1)
data.labels: never passed to fit(), scalers, imputers, calibrators or thresholds

score_cache.note: key = hash of detector params, KNN/LOF fit sample size, preprocessing, PyOD version and the ECOD variant

metrics.computed_on: test window only (ADBench test split, ULB day 2, each IEEE-CIS month 2-6)
metrics.recall_tolerance: unused: recall is reported, with no criterion attached

evaluation.seeds: every method containing IForest is run with seeds 0-4 (an ensemble is fused once per seed, other members unchanged); its metrics are the mean over the 5 seeds
evaluation.budget_mode_runs: the four ensembles x six fusion configs and the six singles, at every budget of the dataset
evaluation.median_single: median of the six singles' seed-mean FP@K at the same budget and window (with six values: the mean of the 3rd and 4th)
evaluation.regret: FP@K(method) - FP@K(oracle_best_single), same budget and window

statistics.delta: dFP@K = FP@K(ensemble) - FP@K(comparator), same budget and window

bootstrap.ulb: transaction-level: day-2 rows resampled with replacement, same size
bootstrap.ieee_cis: day-block: whole days of the test window resampled with replacement
bootstrap.paired: the same resample for every method and seed
bootstrap.scores: fixed; nothing is refitted; K recomputed from the resample size

statistics.criterion: 'fewer false alarms' only if the 95% CI of dFP@K lies entirely below 0; otherwise 'no difference shown'
statistics.adbench: Friedman + Nemenyi CD (alpha 0.05); Wilcoxon signed-rank for ensemble vs median single, Holm-corrected

H1a.budget: primary budget of each dataset (ULB 0.002, IEEE-CIS 0.02)
H1a.supported_if: the criterion holds on both datasets

H1b.budget: primary budget of each dataset (ULB 0.002, IEEE-CIS 0.02)
H1b.supported_if: the criterion holds on at least one dataset

H2b.primary: degenerate: the 2% rule selected E-lit, so E-bench vs E-lit has dFP@K = 0 by identity (benchmark selection confirms the literature default); reported as such
H2b.secondary: E-bench-5% vs E-lit at the primary budget of each dataset, same criterion; descriptive only

H3a.comparator: median of the six singles' values of the same measure (IForest seed mean)
H3a.measure: mean over months 2-6 of |monthly alert rate - (1 - q)|
H3a.supported_if: the 95% day-block bootstrap CI of the difference (ensemble - median single) lies entirely below 0

hypotheses.other_results: E-all, E-bench-5%, the sensitivity fusion configs, the other budgets and quantiles: descriptive, no claim

baselines.default_iforest: IForest with the PyOD defaults above, seed-mean metrics: the realistic practitioner pick
baselines.oracle_best_single: per budget and window, the single detector with the lowest seed-mean FP@K on the test window, chosen with test labels: an upper bound, not a deployable method
